<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:airbnb-ebr" data-paper-title="Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-airbnb-ebr-a90e62e0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7de56d9be73fcab">Why combine query/listing towers with geography and inventory filters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aairbnb-ebr">Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dot-product retrieval finds relevant homes, but availability and destination remain request-specific constraints. An index accelerates matching without making eligibility inferable from similarity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A highly relevant apartment can be in the wrong city or unavailable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06873">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7de56d9be73fcab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:airbnb-ebr" data-paper-title="Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b96313817395d985">Why build hard negatives from search, browsing, and booking journeys?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aairbnb-ebr">Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random listings often differ obviously by geography or conditions. Browsed but unbooked listings are closer decision alternatives, though not necessarily disliked; explain sampling and retain serving filters/versioning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Within a Paris trip, similar local listings are harder than Tokyo, but sold-out homes are not necessarily irrelevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06873">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b96313817395d985">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:airbnb-ebr" data-paper-title="Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-03cce997a8ff19b3">How does traffic replay differ from static negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aairbnb-ebr">Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay reconstructs real requests, journey candidates, and filters; static negatives may be too easy. Replay better matches first-stage competition but not live feedback or changing inventory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distinguish New York listings available on matching dates, not just New York versus nationwide random homes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06873">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03cce997a8ff19b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:airbnb-ebr" data-paper-title="Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7ceaa141a992d9f">How match hard negatives and eligible candidates with targets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aairbnb-ebr">Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use a positive from the same request and reasonable unselected journey listings in the contrastive denominator. Keep serving versions consistent. Local movie proxies lack inventory/geography.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two viewed but unbooked nearby homes are harder than an unavailable home in another city.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06873">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7ceaa141a992d9f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:allecompanion" data-paper-title="Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-allecompanion-f53aba66" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-db05219008dd977e">Why build ComCat relations before category-constrained towers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aallecompanion">Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Allegro.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rules, people, LMs, and statistics define plausible complementary categories. Towers/adapters learn item-level matches within them. A category prior does not guarantee compatibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cameras and lenses complement each other, but mounts still need matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.05063-allecompanion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db05219008dd977e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:allecompanion" data-paper-title="Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2957cba162130ef2">Why can strongly co-occurring products be poor complements?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aallecompanion">Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Allegro.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Co-occurrence can reflect comparison or popularity. Complements jointly serve a need. Category evidence and adapters constrain compatibility without reading hidden target category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Comparing two cameras does not make them complements; a compatible lens may be.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.05063-allecompanion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2957cba162130ef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:allecompanion" data-paper-title="Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a2ad12c1c72b9db">How does complementary retrieval differ from similar-item retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aallecompanion">Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Allegro.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similarity finds substitutes; complement retrieval finds functionally related items used together. Next-item hits are not true complement labels, so local Amazon negatives do not alone refute ComCat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Another tent is a substitute; a sleeping bag complements a tent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.05063-allecompanion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a2ad12c1c72b9db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:allecompanion" data-paper-title="Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-26fc233a12d9d993">Can Category Adapter inference read the hidden target category?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aallecompanion">Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Allegro.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Evaluate all candidate categories using their own features and train on allowed train pairs. Local data lacks true ComCat labels, so keep diagnostic status and negative outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Telling the model the answer is a lens bypasses category selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.05063-allecompanion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26fc233a12d9d993">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:asarl" data-paper-title="ASARL: Autonomous Social-Aware Relevance Learning for QQ Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-asarl-181d0e5f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c546964529a7273">Why learn three social relevance levels before distilling an online student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aasarl">ASARL: Autonomous Social-Aware Relevance Learning for QQ Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent PCG</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Colloquial, long-tail titles need contextual teacher supervision. Transfer fine-grained label distributions to a small model; validate against real search needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>“Weekend group” can mean gaming or hiking; teacher reasons in context and student predicts strong, weak, or irrelevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26593-asarl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c546964529a7273">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:asarl" data-paper-title="ASARL: Autonomous Social-Aware Relevance Learning for QQ Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bf061e90f455235">Why not replace ASARL Critic and GenAgent with one LLM labeling pass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aasarl">ASARL: Autonomous Social-Aware Relevance Learning for QQ Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent PCG</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A one-pass labeler can inherit bias and miss long-tail intent. ReasonAgent proposes, Critic finds repeated gaps, GenAgent targets them, and behavior feedback plus distillation adapts serving. Generated rationales are not automatically truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Diagnose campus-slang mistakes, then add matching counterexamples rather than more unrelated labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26593-asarl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bf061e90f455235">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:asarl" data-paper-title="ASARL: Autonomous Social-Aware Relevance Learning for QQ Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-36bcca6a95183b32">How does PGO differ from synthetic three-level supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aasarl">ASARL: Autonomous Social-Aware Relevance Learning for QQ Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent PCG</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>PGO uses interaction-validated reasoning/label preference pairs, not only generated and reviewed labels. Behavior can remain biased; lower classification loss is not retrieval evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Real users preferring camera-model groups can correct generic photography labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26593-asarl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36bcca6a95183b32">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:asarl" data-paper-title="ASARL: Autonomous Social-Aware Relevance Learning for QQ Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f737fc745ada373a">Does ASARL KL distill reasons or label distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aasarl">ASARL: Autonomous Social-Aware Relevance Learning for QQ Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent PCG</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The online student minimizes teacher/student label-distribution KL. Reasons support data and teacher training, not online explanations. Genre proxy classification improved without ranking transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn three relevance probabilities rather than generate long reasoning per request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26593-asarl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f737fc745ada373a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:beque" data-paper-title="Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-beque-26cd2487" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3063f4740daf0113">Why not evaluate BEQUE rewrites only by their textual similarity to human rewrites?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abeque">Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar wording does not guarantee relevance, coverage, or hits in the retrieved item set. BEQUE scores self-sampled rewrites using a real search system and trains the generator on the induced preferences. Improvements in the chosen composite feedback do not guarantee that all metrics improve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A polished rewrite of a damp-proof camping query into outdoor lifestyle can lose sleeping-mat results. Inspect the retrieval, not the wording alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03758">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2311.03758-beque/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3063f4740daf0113">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:beque" data-paper-title="Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ca47927da463164">Why does BEQUE apply PRO to multiple self-sampled rewrites after SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abeque">Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT learns demonstration rewrites, not necessarily their retrieval effects. BEQUE samples several candidates for each query, builds a preference ordering from offline search feedback, and uses length-normalized sequence scores to learn relative quality. The feedback combines objectives such as relevance and incremental recall; a composite win can hide a component regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two fluent rewrites may differ because one retrieves only existing popular items and the other adds relevant long-tail items. Search feedback detects that difference; also check incremental coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03758">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2311.03758-beque/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ca47927da463164">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:beque" data-paper-title="Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b2761f870e80195">How does BEQUE&#x27;s PRO supervision differ from continuing SFT only on the best rewrite?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abeque">Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Winner-only SFT discards relations among other candidates for the same query. PRO contrasts ranked candidates successively, teaching probability ordering across quality levels while retaining SFT for stability. Length normalization and temperature affect the comparison, and the feedback design still limits what a composite improvement means.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With four ordered rewrites, winner-only SFT imitates the first; PRO additionally learns that the second beats the third and the third beats the fourth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03758">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2311.03758-beque/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b2761f870e80195">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:beque" data-paper-title="Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8125c6476f377c2e">Why must BEQUE&#x27;s local PRO ordering exclude human SFT targets from its candidates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abeque">Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Alignment evaluates actual model-generated rewrites. Inserting a gold target introduces an answer the generator might not have produced, changing the experiment. Use model candidates and a label-free fallback, rank by catalog feedback, and isolate training and test preference sets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If all four beams miss the right category, report that feedback; injecting the correct rewrite and selecting it disguises a generation failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03758">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2311.03758-beque/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8125c6476f377c2e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:capts" data-paper-title="CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-capts-e4a04e24" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2ae5faa63b3569c">Why define CAPTS trigger value after the two-hop retrieval chain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acapts">CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A trigger retrieves other content; its clicks need not predict the value of those candidates. VAM attributes downstream consumption back to the entry point within its I2I channel; CATR allocates routes for complementary coverage. Trigger value depends on the downstream channel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A popular watched video may yield redundant candidates, while an obscure history item surfaces a new topic the user likes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12564">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12564-capts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2ae5faa63b3569c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:capts" data-paper-title="CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-696381a02e76aa05">Why does CAPTS value a trigger through downstream content consumption instead of trigger clicks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acapts">CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A trigger is an entry point, and its direct feedback may not describe what it retrieves. VAM attributes consumption of two-hop content to the trigger; CATR jointly assigns triggers to I2I channels while rewarding value and penalizing overlap. Popular entry points can waste limited candidate slots by returning the same content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two popular triggers retrieve the same comedy videos, while a less popular one adds valuable science videos. Value and complementarity can guide a better allocation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12564">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12564-capts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-696381a02e76aa05">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:capts" data-paper-title="CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d510fa145843a7c">How does CAPTS joint channel routing differ from selecting the strongest trigger for each I2I channel independently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acapts">CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent optimization can send every channel through the same trigger and produce overlapping sets. The joint objective balances downstream value against overlap to allocate distinct roles. Coverage may trade against precision; the reported task measurements are not proof of cost-free improvement across every channel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rather than retrieving the same popular sequels three times, let one channel keep them and another explore related work through director interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12564">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12564-capts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d510fa145843a7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:capts" data-paper-title="CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f638ca3d8dc3d29">Why retain trigger, channel, and downstream item indexes when aggregating CAPTS value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acapts">CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same trigger can return different candidates and contributions by channel. Attribute weights and feedback to the correct path and use it to compute channel overlap during joint selection. A global item score loses trigger credit. Public proxy consumption labels are not production value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When two triggers retrieve the same item, do not credit each with the entire consumption event. Keep path and weight to identify what each trigger actually added.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12564">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12564-capts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f638ca3d8dc3d29">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cluster-goobs" data-paper-title="Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cluster-goobs-3f572e40" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-96b235575e77219f">Why change Cluster GOOBS&#x27;s training negative pool rather than the online model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acluster-goobs">Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The two-tower similarity is unchanged. The training denominator sees harder competitors from a live semantic cluster pool; serving requires no new scorer. The changed learning distribution should be assessed on the full catalog, not just a similarly sampled subset.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train a camera positive against similar camera or lens negatives while serving the same two-tower vector index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.00448-cluster-goobs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96b235575e77219f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cluster-goobs" data-paper-title="Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6937b4d52e6ff1ef">Why does Cluster GOOBS mostly draw negatives from the positive&#x27;s semantic cluster but keep random negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acluster-goobs">Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same-cluster items are closer to the decision boundary than easy random negatives; random draws preserve global coverage. The change is segmented maintenance and sampling in the live out-of-batch pool, not adding an online LLM. Same-cluster items can be false negatives, so validate the ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Other running shoes are harder negatives than refrigerators, but occasional cross-category draws preserve broader distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.00448-cluster-goobs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6937b4d52e6ff1ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cluster-goobs" data-paper-title="Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c2cb8a9fc3232c5">What does Cluster GOOBS add beyond hard negatives from the current batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acluster-goobs">Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A continuously updated out-of-batch pool is larger and less subject to current batch size and chance; semantic segments keep sampling manageable. Balance stale vectors and false negatives with random draws. Constant sampling cost is not constant total training complexity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A batch may lack comparable movies; a cross-batch pool has same-genre options, some of which can be false negatives the user would like.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.00448-cluster-goobs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c2cb8a9fc3232c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cluster-goobs" data-paper-title="Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cdff540d8f7eb8cc">How should Cluster GOOBS avoid test leakage in its random-to-cluster ratio and live-pool updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acluster-goobs">Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Build clusters and pools from training-available content and interactions; fix the ratio by design or validation, not repeated test hits. The limited local MovieLens transition proxy uses genres, not the original multimodal clusters. Full-catalog evaluation is separate from the pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 1:15 mixture does not mean testing only 16 items, and test targets must not enter pool updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.00448-cluster-goobs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cdff540d8f7eb8cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:core-relevance" data-paper-title="CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-core-relevance-f3a9a752" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff961451ea4c9ef2">Why are CORE&#x27;s High, Mid, and Low not simply unordered categories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acore-relevance">CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan / Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High emphasizes strict entity and intent match; Mid versus Low distinguishes acceptable substitutes from unrelated results. Different criteria and error costs motivate conditional heads, but ordering does not imply equally spaced numerical targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The requested phone model is High, a suitable alternative may be Mid, and an unrelated accessory may be Low.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24417-core-relevance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff961451ea4c9ef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:core-relevance" data-paper-title="CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b18203bd21d4b568">Why does CORE classify High versus Non-High first, then distinguish Mid and Low only for Non-High?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acore-relevance">CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan / Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordered labels have different boundaries; a flat three-way classifier conflates exact matching with looser substitution. Conditional heads specialize, and step rewards apply only to executed steps. High examples must not produce a Mid/Low step gradient. Aggregate teacher probabilities correctly in distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>First check exact model match; only a non-match requires deciding whether it is substitutable or unrelated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24417-core-relevance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b18203bd21d4b568">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:core-relevance" data-paper-title="CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16957d65af880b23">How does CORE step-GRPO allocate credit differently from one reward for the final class?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acore-relevance">CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan / Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final reward cannot identify the first judgment, the conditional second step, or format as the source of error. Step rewards normalize within groups for valid steps, masking Mid/Low after High. Credit depends on verifiable steps, not on longer reasoning text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct High decision should not force a Mid/Low response or ambiguous updates to a step that never ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24417-core-relevance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16957d65af880b23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:core-relevance" data-paper-title="CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-008971e4da77f9dd">Why does CORE distillation use logsumexp for the Non-High teacher logit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acore-relevance">CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan / Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Non-High combines Mid and Low probabilities, so use `log(exp z_M + exp z_L)`, not their logit mean. The second head compares only Mid and Low with aligned masks and conditional labels. Copying three logits into both heads changes their meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two substantial Mid and Low probabilities can together exceed High; averaging logits misses their combined mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24417-core-relevance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-008971e4da77f9dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:crsd" data-paper-title="From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-crsd-bbd3991b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-94dea0d87b1d446e">Why is reasoning a training augmentation in CRSD rather than a permanent serving requirement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acrsd">From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rationales can enrich supervision but cost real-time generation. A student learns from plain and rationale-augmented views, transferring augmented-view distributions to the plain path. This does not guarantee retention of complete reasoning or faithful explanations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train with a commuting-lightweight rationale, but serve on current features without first generating a long explanation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11056">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.11056-crsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94dea0d87b1d446e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:crsd" data-paper-title="From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3ef068bf8e66afc1">Why does CRSD compare reasoning and no-reasoning views in one student instead of serving reasoning chains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acrsd">From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The reasoning view offers richer relationships; the plain view is the low-latency input used in production. Self-distillation and contrastive learning transfer judgment to the plain path while label supervision anchors correctness. Leaked answers or view distribution mismatch can make a lower loss misleading.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train relevance with an attribute-comparison rationale, then require similar decisions from query and item alone without generating a rationale per candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11056">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.11056-crsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3ef068bf8e66afc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:crsd" data-paper-title="From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16dedeae125cf8d6">How does CRSD&#x27;s contrastive self-distillation differ from fitting external teacher logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acrsd">From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One lightweight student produces distributions under both views, and a contrastive loss also constrains representations. Shared parameters can reduce scale mismatch but do not eliminate erroneous rationales. Check actual gradient and stop-gradient paths rather than assuming self-distillation is unbiased.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same model reads ordinary product information and an augmented rationale; a separate fixed teacher would not share its parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11056">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.11056-crsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16dedeae125cf8d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:crsd" data-paper-title="From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c70d8635c52695c">Why would appending reasoning r at serving violate CRSD&#x27;s distillation objective?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acrsd">From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The plain `pS(·|x)` learns from augmented `pS(·|x,r)` specifically to remove online rationale generation. Requiring r restores cost and does not verify plain-path learning. Test training losses and rationale-free inference separately; local proxies do not verify full domain LLM training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generating rationales before scoring tests the augmented pipeline; serving only raw x tests the intended lightweight path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11056">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.11056-crsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c70d8635c52695c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cs3" data-paper-title="CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cs3-e2cd1a82" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c2970df359ab633">Why is interaction in CS3 a trade-off between retrieval efficiency and expressivity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acs3">CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent towers enable precomputed item vectors and one user vector for nearest-neighbor retrieval. Deep interactions usually depend on pairs and cannot be globally cached. Cyclic refinement and knowledge collaboration add links while respecting deployment boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If each user&#x27;s item vector differed, a single shared index could not serve it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19269">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.19269-cs3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c2970df359ab633">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cs3" data-paper-title="CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f1f4ef09f0f9947">Why can&#x27;t CS3 write candidate vectors back into all shared user representations to strengthen interaction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acs3">CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Efficient two-tower retrieval needs independently computed user and item vectors. Candidate-specific user states cannot retrieve the full catalog with one query. CS3 uses deployable cyclic refinement and knowledge collaboration; track which updates are offline-materializable and which depend on candidates. Training interactions are not free ANN features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding item A&#x27;s details can improve scoring A but makes the vector unsuitable as the same query for B and C.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19269">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.19269-cs3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f1f4ef09f0f9947">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cs3" data-paper-title="CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-310a5a6284b81045">How does CS3 gated residual refinement differ from replacing the two towers with a cross-encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acs3">CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gated residuals make controlled updates around the two-tower state and use collaborative losses while retaining the serving interface. Cross-encoders jointly encode each pair. Their compute and index dependencies differ; the matched local result was negative, so quality preservation is not established.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bounded correction to a retrievable vector is cheaper and structurally different from re-encoding every user-item pair from scratch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19269">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.19269-cs3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-310a5a6284b81045">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cs3" data-paper-title="CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a29682928ab8d584">How should CS3 cyclic refinement distinguish offline item state from online candidate-dependent state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acs3">CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trace whether an update reads the current user or candidate; downstream tensors are no longer global cache values. Match gate and residual dimensions and specify previous versus current iteration state, avoiding accidental in-place semantics. Preserve the actual cycle, cross-sync, and loss paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refining item i for user A must not overwrite the generic vector read by user B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19269">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.19269-cs3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a29682928ab8d584">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:elise" data-paper-title="Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-elise-a73bc968" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e99e6ece1c058781">Why keep lexical and semantic retrieval in ELISE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aelise">Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lexical search handles exact entities, model IDs, and constraints; dual encoders handle paraphrase and semantic association. Calibrate scores and cap semantic results so broad matches do not override explicit requirements. Either path can still err.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search a specific camera model lexically, while semantic retrieval can find waterproof gear for rainy hikes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10239">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.10239-elise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e99e6ece1c058781">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:elise" data-paper-title="Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67a17072942f12de">Why quantile-match before fusing semantic and lexical scores in ELISE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aelise">Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw scores differ in scale and distribution, so a wide-range scorer can dominate. Map each score to its relative distribution position, fuse under controls, and limit semantic result count. Percentiles are not click probabilities and do not replace exact-entity checks; language shifts can require recalibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lexical scores in the tens would swamp cosine scores near 0–1; percentile matching balances them while preserving exact song-title controls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10239">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.10239-elise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67a17072942f12de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:elise" data-paper-title="Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb8bb8bb0fe59c3a">How does quantile matching differ from min-max scaling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aelise">Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Min-max primarily adjusts range; quantiles map positions in empirical distributions and can align different shapes. Equal percentiles are not equal relevance probabilities and drift changes their meaning. Equal numeric ranges do not establish probability calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A heavy lexical tail and narrow semantic distribution may not align by multiplying by a constant; novel queries can still violate old empirical distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10239">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.10239-elise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb8bb8bb0fe59c3a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:elise" data-paper-title="Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-96f620f321725996">Why lock ELISE&#x27;s mapping, fusion weights, and semantic quota before test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aelise">Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each changes candidates and ranks. Fit them on training or validation, freeze them for test, and use the same serving quota. Do not hide negative proxy results by selecting the best test mix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing 70% semantic after examining test makes the report optimistic; lock the ratio and mapping before evaluating new requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10239">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.10239-elise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96f620f321725996">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:friend-gnn" data-paper-title="Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-friend-gnn-0f3bf9e0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-608c9a7e5fd4b8a6">Why address both user-ID storage and temporal edge visibility in Friend-GNN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afriend-gnn">Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI VK</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Massive graphs make per-user tables expensive; shared hashes compress identities. Edges after prediction expose outcomes, so constrain time separately before GNN propagation. Neither property establishes recommendation accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A billion users can share hash tables, but predicting yesterday still cannot sample today&#x27;s friend links.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.27413-friend-gnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-608c9a7e5fd4b8a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:friend-gnn" data-paper-title="Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-991287c8e490534e">Why does Friend-GNN need both multi-hash user representations and temporal-prefix neighbor sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afriend-gnn">Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI VK</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-hash tables reduce storage but do not prevent time leakage. Temporal CSR sorts edges so queries sample only pre-cutoff neighbors before graph aggregation. Verify memory and observational legality separately from ranking scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tuesday&#x27;s friend recommendation cannot use Friday&#x27;s new connection, no matter how compact the user embeddings are.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.27413-friend-gnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-991287c8e490534e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:friend-gnn" data-paper-title="Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
