<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d0825584eb05ffd">Why do three independent concatenated hashes mitigate rather than eliminate collisions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afriend-gnn">Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI VK</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single hash gives same-bucket users one embedding. Multiple addresses reduce the chance all buckets match, and projection combines them. Partial sharing and complete collisions remain; this is not an independent ID table.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two users with the same first bucket can differ in the other two, but identical triples remain indistinguishable by this encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.27413-friend-gnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d0825584eb05ffd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:friend-gnn" data-paper-title="Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f8d5d303c99adcd3">Why sort per-user neighbor times before taking a historical prefix in temporal CSR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afriend-gnn">Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI VK</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Binary search needs sorted timestamps to locate cutoff `τ−Δ`, then sample only its legal prefix. Use `lower_bound` semantics to determine cutoff inclusion rather than claiming the current full graph was filtered.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unsorted January, February, and March edges can cause a binary search for a February cutoff to admit March.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.27413-friend-gnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f8d5d303c99adcd3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genfacet" data-paper-title="GenFacet: End-to-End Generative Faceted Search via Multi-Task Preference Alignment in E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-genfacet-00b00c8d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e2cea1f051265fa">Why treat GenFacet facet selection and query rewriting as one search pipeline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenfacet">GenFacet: End-to-End Generative Faceted Search via Multi-Task Preference Alignment in E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A facet determines the refinement, and the rewrite turns it into a retrievable query. Independent optimization can produce attractive facets with no results or drift from intent. Joint retrieval feedback depends on catalog and reward reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Commuting can refine a query toward light, waterproof products, not specialist off-road equipment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19665-genfacet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e2cea1f051265fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genfacet" data-paper-title="GenFacet: End-to-End Generative Faceted Search via Multi-Task Preference Alignment in E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c5bc783ab3fe2880">Why jointly optimize GenFacet facet generation and query rewriting on downstream retrieval feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenfacet">GenFacet: End-to-End Generative Faceted Search via Multi-Task Preference Alignment in E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Plausible facet text can yield poor search, and rewrites must preserve intent under the selected facet. Multitask preference alignment uses facet quality and actual retrieval results to avoid mismatched local goals. Feedback can favor popular facets; fluency or one hit metric is insufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lightweight-laptop weight facet should yield a searchable weight constraint, not a fluent rewrite about performance rankings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19665-genfacet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c5bc783ab3fe2880">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genfacet" data-paper-title="GenFacet: End-to-End Generative Faceted Search via Multi-Task Preference Alignment in E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3692d7096617bcd7">How does GenFacet multitask preference alignment differ from text-only teacher distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenfacet">GenFacet: End-to-End Generative Faceted Search via Multi-Task Preference Alignment in E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text distillation copies teacher wording. Multitask rewards score the facet and retrieved results, correcting fluent but useless choices while potentially neglecting unmeasured constraints. Negative local results cannot be replaced by production design goals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Machine washable may retrieve useful items where an elegant lifestyle phrase does not, but easy keyword hits can also game the reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19665-genfacet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3692d7096617bcd7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genfacet" data-paper-title="GenFacet: End-to-End Generative Faceted Search via Multi-Task Preference Alignment in E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b7f66fb276b673f">Why preserve facet-to-rewrite correspondence in GenFacet training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenfacet">GenFacet: End-to-End Generative Faceted Search via Multi-Task Preference Alignment in E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval credit belongs to the context and facet that produced that query. Define task weights, reference policy, and valid-output masks. Deterministic candidate scores without actual generation and updates do not establish teacher distillation plus GRPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Credit a successful waterproof query to its own facet, not a lightweight facet.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19665-genfacet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b7f66fb276b673f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hap" data-paper-title="Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hap-86607d9e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8556d538b0f73ee2">Why does HAP allocate light or strong pre-ranking by candidate difficulty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahap">Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Toutiao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Easy negatives need little compute, while ambiguous candidates benefit from more interactions. Routing has cost and can err, sending important items to the light branch. Dynamic budgeting is not simply extra work for popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Quickly reject clearly irrelevant products and compare two nearly identical eligible products with the strong model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03770-hap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8556d538b0f73ee2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hap" data-paper-title="Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-886b08d0b9de067d">Why harmonize HAP scores after routing difficult candidates to the strong branch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahap">Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Toutiao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Branch compute differs and raw score distributions may not be comparable. Difficulty routing allocates work and harmonization aligns rankings across branches. Misrouting can still lose key items, so measure ranking quality alongside compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A light branch averaging 0.8 would unfairly dominate a strong branch averaging 0.4 without scale alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03770-hap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-886b08d0b9de067d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hap" data-paper-title="Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-26201eaaf777f09a">What cross-path relation does HAP harmonization address beyond calibrating only the strong branch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahap">Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Toutiao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Items from both paths compete in one ranking; internal accuracy is insufficient. Harmonization aligns score scales and preferences across budgets to prevent route identity becoming an advantage. It can limit specialization, so measure cost and quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A simple candidate scored 0.8 should not automatically beat a difficult valuable one scored 0.4 by a different branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03770-hap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26201eaaf777f09a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hap" data-paper-title="Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-db25c552897fed6f">Why distinguish soft HAP training from actual compute budgets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahap">Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Toutiao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Soft mixtures can execute both branches even when a gate is near zero or one. Hard serving routes need explicit thresholds and fallbacks; local ranking proxies do not measure production latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Running both networks then multiplying by a binary gate changes output but saves no FLOPs; verify the inactive branch actually does not run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03770-hap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db25c552897fed6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harness-lm" data-paper-title="HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-harness-lm-9919eb79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-71f6c9ca8eea9645">Why can HARNESS-LM use a large offline document encoder and a small online query encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharness-lm">HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft AI / Bing Ads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Document work is amortized through reuse, while live queries are encoded on demand. Align the student query space, then refine against frozen documents. A smaller student can still lose complex intent distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Precompute a million ad vectors overnight while processing each live query in milliseconds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23572">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.23572-harness-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-71f6c9ca8eea9645">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harness-lm" data-paper-title="HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d02a310dcb03bd2f">Why freeze the strong document tower during HARNESS-LM refinement and train only the small query encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharness-lm">HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft AI / Bing Ads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Document vectors can be precomputed; query encoding is latency-sensitive. Align the small tower to the teacher query space, then contrastively refine in the fixed document space to avoid index drift and costly rebuilds. Freezing limits adaptation and does not guarantee teacher quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student searches an existing million-ad coordinate system instead of changing it and invalidating the index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23572">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.23572-harness-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d02a310dcb03bd2f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harness-lm" data-paper-title="HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7582077c51c0e0b">Why are HARNESS-LM L2 alignment and subsequent InfoNCE refinement not redundant?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharness-lm">HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft AI / Bing Ads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>L2 initializes query coordinates close to the teacher; InfoNCE directly distinguishes relevant from competing fixed documents rather than minimizing coordinate error. Local loss convergence alongside retrieval regression shows that these are distinct signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A vector closer to the teacher can still misorder similar ads; contrastive refinement explicitly compares them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23572">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.23572-harness-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7582077c51c0e0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harness-lm" data-paper-title="HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2614230fc91437a1">Why verify no teacher document gradients during HARNESS-LM refinement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharness-lm">HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft AI / Bing Ads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen document tower preserves the existing index while the student adapts. Changing documents invalidates the no-rebuild contract. Check gradients or parameter fingerprints rather than optimizer names, and do not infer online index deployment from alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After one step query parameters may change but document parameters must not; moving document vectors breaks an old index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
